open_obligations: Check whether the capability gap between debaters and judges is information access rather than model capability, and whether Khan et al. list this as a limitation.
Check whether ground truth is used only for evaluation, as sandwiching requires.
Check whether any model is aligned or fine-tuned in an inner loop.
in.other_title: Human judges 88% with debate vs 78% consultancy; LLM judges 76% vs 54% (naive 60% / 48%)
in.rationale: Bowman et al. ask whether debate can be validated empirically under sandwiching. Khan et al. report that, for the most persuasive models, non-expert human judges reach 88% with LLM debate versus 60% naive and 78% consultancy, in an information-asymmetric setup.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate between LLMs helps non-expert judges beyond a baseline, in an information-asymmetric QuALITY HARD setup

open_obligations: Check whether debate and market-making use the same number of turns.
Note that the supervisor is a model, not a non-expert human as in sandwiching.
Check that the four tasks have a strong-weak gap large enough for a sandwiching analogy.
in.other_title: Debate beats consultancy and market-making on test accuracy and PGR across four tasks
in.rationale: Bowman et al. ask for empirical trials of debate and market-making. Lang, Huang and Li report that debate used in their approach performs better than all other variants, including market-making and consultancy, in test accuracy and PGR across all four tasks, at least in their settings; the 'weak supervisor' is a model, not a human.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate and market-making differ as sources of information for a weak supervisor, across the four tasks Lang, Huang and Li test

open_obligations: Check whether the setup counts as sandwiching given that experts are humans, not a model more capable than the non-experts.
Note that no model is trained or aligned in the inner loop.
Check how ground-truth labels are used for evaluation versus Bowman et al.'s expert outer loop.
in.other_title: Debate beats consultancy for non-expert judges: 84% vs 74% on hard reading comprehension questions
in.rationale: Bowman et al. call for empirical trials of debate under sandwiching. Michael et al. have non-expert judges who cannot read the passage judge debates between experts who can, reporting 84% for debate versus 74% for consultancy; the 'model' is often a human expert and there is no fine-tuning loop, so it is a relaxed sandwiching test.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate helps non-experts supervise better-informed experts, in a sandwiching-like setup on QuALITY-hard

text: The authors say the paper introduces a research paradigm that represents an attempt to make concrete the sandwiching proposal first outlined in Cotra (2021), and that its results establish that scalable oversight techniques can be productively evaluated on existing NLP task datasets. They say it lays out a roadmap and that they are eager to see empirical trials of techniques like debate, market-making and recursive reward modeling.
title: Do debate, market-making and recursive reward modeling work in sandwiching trials?
